acceptance: Source-policy/filter identity and synthetic stdlib enforcement tests precede measurement; actual owned process enforcement/status and observed affinities must match. This proves CPU execution constraints, not semantic quality, benchmark improvement or model calibration.
kernel_boundary: A successful process-local no_new_privs seccomp filter is inherited across exec/clone and cannot be removed by the child; native sched_setaffinity attempts remain EPERM, retaining the inheritedCPU0/1 bound. Only claim the supported ABI/kernel behavior actually tested and observed.
network_scope_unchanged: Network restrictions remain Python/Node public API interposition plus source review; no OS-enforced network syscall isolation is claimed.
reason: Taskset/environment settings alone do not prevent a native runtime from changing thread affinity. Enforce the authorized CPU0/1 bound without changing immutable model/code options.
required_sequence: Require actual Linux x86_64 execution and exact source/policy/owner admission. Fail closed if unsupported.
Set/verify initial owned worker and native child affinity exactly CPUs0,1 before native addon import.

Before Node exec, set no_new_privs and install a process-local seccomp BPF filter which refuses sched_setaffinity (x86_64 syscall203) with EPERM. Enforce the declared architecture and disallow alternate ABI bypass; installation/architecture failures abort before model initialization.

Preserve all original submitted Native104 code, assets, constructor/model options and prediction inputs. Apply no head-fitting, model-thread option changes, affinity repairs or retries after an actual start.

Read native process NoNewPrivs/Seccomp/filter-count status and observed task/thread affinities after initialization and at saved progress checkpoints. Record original actual OS thread counts; do not assert Threads==2.
Any observed affinity outside0,1 or missing/failed required enforcement proof rejects qualification. Observed snapshot scope does not imply continuous observation of every short-lived thread.
Preserve native stderr, including any original runtime affinity warnings, without changing a response or hiding failure. A refused affinity syscall is the prospective CPU policy, not a network event.
scope: Only the newly owned Node native child and its descendants/threads, before exec and before any original native addon/model initialization; no host or unrelated process changes.
